'''Pierre Deshawn Jackson''' (born August 29, 1991) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Al Ittihad Alexandria (basketball)|Al Ittihad Alexandria]] of the [[Egyptian Basketball Premier League]]. He played college basketball for the [[College of Southern Idaho]] and [[Baylor University]] in which he was one of the top college players in the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13 season]]. Following stints in Europe and the [[NBA G League|NBA D-League]], Jackson played one season in the [[NBA]] with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].

==High school and junior college career==
Jackson attended [[Desert Pines High School]] in Las Vegas. Following a standout career, where he led the state of Nevada in assists as a senior, he went to the [[College of Southern Idaho]] (CSI). At CSI, Jackson led the Golden Eagles to a [[National Junior College Athletic Association]] (NJCAA) [[NJCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|National Championship]] in 2011, earning tournament MVP honors.  He averaged 18.6 [[Points per game|points]] and 4.4 [[assists per game]] in 2010–11 and was named a first-team All-American and the NJCAA Player of the Year at the conclusion of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://athletics.csi.edu/news/2011/4/15/MBB_0415114228.aspx?path=mbball|title=CSI head coach and player earn national honors|work=CSI.edu|publisher=CSI Athletics|date=April 15, 2011|access-date=November 16, 2012}}</ref>

==College career==
After concluding his junior college career, Jackson moved to [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]] to complete his college career.  He had a strong junior campaign for the Bears, averaging 13.8 points and 5.9 assists in the [[2011–12 Baylor Bears basketball team|2011–12 season]].  He helped lead Baylor to the Elite Eight of the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2012 NCAA Tournament]], where they lost to eventual champions [[2011–12 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]]. Jackson was named second team All-[[Big 12 Conference]] and an honorable mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by the [[Associated Press]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=106110&SPID=13134&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=10410&ATCLID=205404258|title=All-America Honors Continue For Big 12 Men's Basketball|work=Big12Sports.com|publisher=[[Big 12 Conference]]|date=March 26, 2012|access-date=November 16, 2012}}</ref>

Jackson returned to Baylor for his senior season in [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13]]. He was named the Big 12 preseason Player of the Year<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=106110&SPID=13134&DB_LANG=C&DB_OEM_ID=10410&ATCLID=205697199|title=Jackson Leads Preseason All-Big 12 Squad|work=Big12Sports.com|publisher=[[Big 12 Conference]]|date=October 4, 2012|access-date=November 16, 2012}}</ref> and was named to the preseason watch lists for the [[Wooden Award|Wooden]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.woodenaward.com/john_r_wooden_award_announces_men_s_preseason_top_50|title=JOHN R. WOODEN AWARD ANNOUNCES MEN'S PRESEASON TOP 50|work=WoodenAward.com|publisher=[[Wooden Award]]|date=November 8, 2012|access-date=November 16, 2012|archive-date=August 18, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190818052833/https://www.woodenaward.com/john_r_wooden_award_announces_men_s_preseason_top_50|url-status=dead}}</ref> and [[Naismith Award|Naismith]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|url=https://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/blog/eye-on-college-basketball/20967590/naismith-announces-early-season-watch-list|title=Naismith announces early-season watch list|work=CBSSports.com|date=November 13, 2012|access-date=November 16, 2012}}</ref> national player of the year awards.

On April 4, 2013, Jackson ended his college career with a championship win over [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]] at the [[National Invitation Tournament]] (NIT).  As a senior, he averaged 19.8 points and 7.1 assists per game.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lynam |first1=Dei |title=Sixers preseason profile: Pierre Jackson |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/philadelphia-sixers/sixers-preseason-profile-pierre-jackson |access-date=April 12, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=September 18, 2014}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===D-League and Turkey===
Jackson was selected with the 42nd overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. On July 12, 2013, his draft rights were traded, along with [[Jrue Holiday]], to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] in exchange for [[Nerlens Noel]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/130712-pelicans-trade|title=Sixers Acquire Rights to Nerlens Noel and a 2014 First-round Pick in Trade With New Orleans|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2013|access-date=July 12, 2013}}</ref> Two days later, he joined the Pelicans for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Cody|last=Williams|url=http://www.rantsports.com/nba/2013/07/14/2013-nba-summer-league-pierre-jackson-will-make-debut-sunday-with-new-orleans-pelicans/|title=2013 NBA Summer League: Pierre Jackson Will Make Debut Sunday with New Orleans Pelicans|work=RantSports.com|date=July 14, 2013|access-date=January 15, 2017|archive-date=January 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170116180742/http://www.rantsports.com/nba/2013/07/14/2013-nba-summer-league-pierre-jackson-will-make-debut-sunday-with-new-orleans-pelicans/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On July 27, 2013, Jackson signed a one-year deal with [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL Villeurbanne]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/104229/asvel-villeurbanne-sign-pierre-jackson.html|title=ASVEL Villeurbanne sign Pierre Jackson|work=Sportando.com|date=July 27, 2013|access-date=July 27, 2013}}</ref> However, he left the team in September 2013 before appearing in a game for them.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/106224/pierre-jackson-leaves-asvel-because-he-is-homesick.html|title=Pierre Jackson leaves ASVEL because he is homesick|work=Sportando.com|date=September 24, 2013|access-date=September 24, 2013}}</ref>

On November 1, 2013, Jackson was selected with the fourth overall pick in the [[2013 NBA Development League Draft|2013 NBA D-League draft]] by the [[Idaho Stampede]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/stampede_draft_pierre_jackson__2013_11_02.html|title=Stampede Draft Pierre Jackson in First Round|work=NBA.com|date=November 1, 2013|access-date=November 1, 2013|url-status=bot: unknown|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610055831/http://www.nba.com/dleague/idaho/stampede_draft_pierre_jackson__2013_11_02.html|archive-date=June 10, 2016}}</ref> On February 3, 2014, he was named to the Futures All-Star roster for the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html|title=Eighth Annual NBA D-League All-Star Game Features 16 Players With NBA Experience|work=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2014|access-date=February 3, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160125213432/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html|archive-date=January 25, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Anthony|last=Oliva|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/allstar2014/pierre_goes_to_nola_2014_02_07.html|title=Pierre goes to New Orleans|work=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2014|access-date=February 3, 2014|url-status=bot: unknown|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610055107/http://www.nba.com/dleague/allstar2014/pierre_goes_to_nola_2014_02_07.html|archive-date=June 10, 2016}}</ref> On February 1, 2014, he recorded a career-high 18 assists in a 127–123 win over the Los Angeles D-Fenders.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2021300213/|title=Los Angeles D-Fenders 123 – Idaho Stampede 127|website=G League |date=February 1, 2014|access-date=March 12, 2020}}</ref> On February 4, 2014, he scored 58 points against the Texas Legends, setting the D-League single-game scoring record. This surpassed the previous record of 53 by [[Morris Almond]] (2008) and [[Will Conroy]] (2009).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20140204/TEXIDA/gameinfo.html|title=JACKSON BREAKS LEAGUE RECORD WITH 58 POINTS IN A 136–122 STAMPEDE WIN OVER TEXAS|work=NBA.com|date=February 4, 2014|access-date=February 5, 2014|url-status=bot: unknown|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140208011142/http://www.nba.com/dleague/games/20140204/TEXIDA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 8, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/10406002/idaho-star-pierre-jackson-scores-d-league-record-58-points|title=Pierre Jackson's 58 D-League best|work=ESPN.com|date=February 4, 2014|access-date=February 5, 2014}}</ref> This effort also established the single-half (2nd) record of 38 points. Although the single-game record was surpassed twice in 2016 (first by [[Jordan McRae]], with 61, and then by [[Russ Smith (basketball)|Russ Smith]], with 65), the single-half record stood until [[Tarik Phillip]] posted 39 in a half on February 24, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/breaking-down-nik-stauskas-wild-57-point-performance|title=Breaking Down Nik Stauskas' Wild Two-Game Stretch|accessdate=May 7, 2022|date=March 3, 2022|work=[[NBA.com]]}}</ref>

On February 20, 2014, Jackson left the Idaho Stampede in order to sign in Turkey.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/111843/pierre-jackson-confirms-he-is-moving-to-fenerbahce.html|title=Pierre Jackson confirms he is moving to Fenerbahce|work=Sportando.com|date=February 20, 2014|access-date=February 20, 2014}}</ref> The next day, he signed with [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe Ülker]] for the rest of the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.bckhimki.ru/news/press/2014/february/1587/|title=FENERBAHCE ULKER bolsters backcourt with rookie Jackson|work=BCKhimki.ru|date=February 21, 2014|access-date=February 22, 2014}}</ref> On April 10, 2014, he parted ways with Fenerbahçe after just six games.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/116692/pierre-jackson-fenerbahce-officially-part-ways.html|title=Pierre Jackson, Fenerbahce officially part ways|work=Sportando.com|date=April 10, 2014|access-date= April 10, 2014}}</ref> He averaged 3.3 points and 1.3 assists over those six games.{{citation needed|date=December 2023}}

On July 15, 2015, Jackson re-signed with the 76ers after averaging 12 points per game in two [[2015 NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]] games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/150714-jackson-signed|title=Sixers Sign Pierre Jackson|work=NBA.com|date=July 15, 2015|access-date=July 15, 2015}}</ref> However, he was later waived by the 76ers on October 26 after appearing in three preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-waive-five|title=PHILADELPHIA 76ERS WAIVE FIVE|work=NBA.com|date=October 26, 2015|access-date=October 26, 2015}}</ref>

===Return to the D-League===
[[Image:Pierre Jackson.jpg|thumb|right|Jackson in July 2016]]
On January 6, 2016, Jackson was reacquired by the Idaho Stampede.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5086704|title=Stampede Re-Acquire Pierre Jackson|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=January 6, 2016|access-date=January 6, 2016}}</ref> He made his season debut for the Stampede three days later in a 98–92 win over the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]], recording six points, one rebound, two assists and one steal in 11 minutes of action off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160109/FWNIDA/|title=Dejean-Jones Leads Strong Defensive Effort in Stampede's Showcase Win|work=NBA.com|date=January 9, 2016|access-date=January 9, 2016}}</ref> On March 4, he was traded to the [[Texas Legends]] in exchange for the returning player rights to [[Eric Griffin (basketball)|Eric Griffin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/legends-acquire-pierre-jackson-in-trade-with-idaho/n-5107433|title=Legends Acquire Pierre Jackson in Trade with Idaho|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=March 4, 2016|access-date=March 4, 2016}}</ref> On March 20, he waived by the Legends before appearing in a game for them.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Texas-Legends/32/Transaction_History/2016/|title=2015–2016 Texas Legends Transactions History|work=RealGM.com|access-date=March 31, 2016}}</ref>

In July 2016, Jackson joined the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-2016-summer-league-roster/|title=TRAIL BLAZERS ANNOUNCE 2016 SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|work=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2016|access-date=October 18, 2016}}</ref>

===Croatia===
On October 18, 2016, Jackson signed a one-month deal with Croatian club [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita Zagreb]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/croatia/214676/kk-cedevita-announces-pierre-jackson.html|title=KK Cedevita announces Pierre Jackson|work=Sportando.com|date=October 18, 2016|access-date=October 18, 2016}}</ref> In his time with Cedevita, he appeared in two [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] games and five [[ABA League]] games.{{citation needed|date=December 2023}}

===Israel===
On July 14, 2017, Jackson signed a one-year deal, with an option for another season, with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7xwgh97wpypdrxcp|title=Maccabi finds scoring power with Jackson|work=EuroLeague.net|date=July 14, 2017|access-date=July 14, 2017}}</ref> In his first Euroleague game for Maccabi, Jackson starred with 27 points, 9 assists and 7 rebounds in an 88–71 win over [[Brose Bamberg]]. He was subsequently named [[2017–18 EuroLeague#MVP of the Round|MVP of Round 1]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/89gxgcciuvqc7op9|title=Round 1 MVP: Pierre Jackson, Maccabi FOX Tel Aviv|work=EuroLeague.net|date=October 14, 2017|access-date=October 14, 2017}}</ref> On March 2, 2018, Jackson participated in the [[2017–18 Israeli Basketball Premier League#All-Star Game|Israeli League All-Star Game]], where he recorded 18 points and 6 assists and was named All-Star Game MVP.<ref>{{cite news|title=אולסטאר: הזרים גברו על הישראלים|url=https://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=17631|work=basket.co.il|date=March 2, 2018|access-date=March 2, 2018|language=he}}</ref> That season, Jackson helped Maccabi to win the [[2017 Israeli Basketball League Cup|Israeli League Cup]] and the [[2018 Israeli Basketball Premier League Final Four|Israeli League Championship]].{{citation needed|date=December 2023}}

===China===
On July 4, 2018, Jackson signed with the [[Beijing Fly Dragons]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Pierre Jackson officially signs with Beijing Flying Dragons|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/asia/china/280154/pierre-jackson-officially-signs-with-beijing-flying-dragons.html|work=Sportando.com|date=July 4, 2018|access-date=July 4, 2018}}{{Dead link|date=March 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> On October 25, 2018, Jackson scored a career-high 67 points (including 10 3-pointers) and 10 assists in a 136–137 loss to the [[Shenzhen Leopards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2018/1025_6546_15106.asp|title=Beijing 136 – Shenzhen 137|publisher=EuroBasket|date=October 25, 2018|access-date=April 12, 2020}}</ref> He left the team in late December 2018.{{citation needed|date=December 2023}}

In July 2019, Jackson signed with the [[Shenzhen Leopards]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Former Mavs guard Pierre Jackson headed to China|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba-news-former-mavs-guard-pierre-jackson-headed-to-china/|work=clutchpoints.com|date=July 17, 2019|access-date=October 22, 2019}}</ref>

===South Bay Lakers===
On January 17, 2020, Jackson was acquired by the [[South Bay Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=South Bay Lakers Acquire Pierre Jackson|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-acquire-pierre-jackson|date=January 17, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 17, 2020|archive-date=September 1, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200901095328/https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-acquire-pierre-jackson/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 29, 2020, he recorded a season-high 38 points including six 3-pointers in a 123–118 win over the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2021900519/|title=Agua Caliente Clippers 113 – South Bay Lakers 118|website=G League |date=February 29, 2020|access-date=March 12, 2020}}</ref>

===Greece===
On August 9, 2020, Jackson officially signed a one-year contract with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Panathinaikos announces Pierre Jackson |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/panathinaikos-announces-pierre-jackson/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 9, 2020 |date=August 9, 2020}}</ref> On September 23, 2020, he played in the semi-final of the [[Greek Basketball Super Cup]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=FIBA LiveStats |url=https://livestats.dcd.shared.geniussports.com/u/ESAKE/1756903/bs.html |access-date=2022-12-19 |website=livestats.dcd.shared.geniussports.com}}</ref> he was injured and left the team on October 13.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jackson leaves Panathinaikos |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Euroleague/news/648442/Jackson-leaves-Panathinaikos |website=Eurobasket |access-date=October 13, 2020 |date=October 13, 2020}}</ref>

===Return to Turkey===
On February 17, 2021, he has signed with [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]] of the Turkish [[Basketball Super League]] (BSL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketfaul.com/haber?haber=92559|title=Eski Fenerbahçeli, Galatasaray'da|last=|first=|date=February 17, 2021|website=|publisher=basketfaul.com|language=Turkish|access-date=February 17, 2021}}</ref>

===France===
On May 11, 2021, he has signed with [[JL Bourg Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/pierre-jackson-signs-with-jl-bourg/|title=Pierre Jackson signs with JL Bourg|last=|first=|date=May 11, 2021|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=May 16, 2021}}</ref>

===Return to South Bay Lakers===
On December 31, 2021, the [[South Bay Lakers]] acquired Jackson. He was then later waived on January 17, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|title=2021–22 NBA G League Transactions|website=gleague.nba.com|date=December 31, 2021|access-date=December 31, 2021}}</ref>

===Return to Turkey===
On January 22, 2022, Jackson signed with [[Afyon Belediye S.K.|HDI Sigorta Afyon Belediye]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Yahyabeyoglu |first1=Fersu |title=Pierre Jackson joins Afyon |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/727839/Pierre-Jackson-joins-Afyon |website=Eurobasket |access-date=January 22, 2022 |date=January 22, 2022}}</ref>

=== Libya ===
On February 22, 2024, Jackson was announced by Libyan club [[Al Ahly Benghazi (basketball)|Al Ahly Ly]] of the [[Basketball Africa League]] (BAL).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hamid Addasi |first=Abdul |date=2024-02-22 |title=Pierre Jackson (ex Nanjing MK) signs at Ahly Benghazi |url=https://www.afrobasket.com/Libya/news/855294/Pierre-Jackson-ex-Nanjing-MK-signs-at-Ahly-Benghazi |access-date=2024-02-23 |work=[[Eurobasket.com|Afrobasket.com]]}}</ref> On April 19, Jackson made his debut with 20 points, 7 rebounds and 11 assists in a 93–71 win over [[Bangui Sporting Club|Bangui]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Al Ahly Ly vs. Bangui SC |url=https://fibalivestats.dcd.shared.geniussports.com/u/BAL/2410678/bs.html |access-date=2024-04-19}}</ref> He left the team before the beginning of the playoffs in May.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-03-23 |title=Final Rosters for the 2024 BAL Playoffs - Who is in, Who is out |url=https://bal.nba.com/news/final-rosters-for-the-2024-bal-playoffs-who-is-in-who-is-out |access-date=2024-05-23 |website=The BAL |language=en}}</ref>
